headline: India tells parliament Hasina not allowed to use Indian soil for political activity
summary: New Delhi reaffirms its policy of not permitting foreign political activities on its territory, while continuing to process Bangladesh's extradition request for the ousted PM.
details: The Indian government has formally stated in the Lok Sabha that ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has not been permitted to use Indian territory for any political activities.
This position was detailed in the response to the 9th report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs, which was tabled in the Indian parliament yesterday.

India maintains a long-standing policy of not allowing its soil to be used for political activities directed against another country, and the government says this policy has been applied to Hasina's case.
Despite this, Hasina has been holding virtual discussions with party leaders and issuing statements in her name, and has given interviews to various media outlets while staying in India.
The Indian government explained that Hasina was allowed to remain in India based on humanitarian grounds, providing refuge to individuals facing imminent threats to life.

Regarding Bangladesh's request for her extradition, the Indian government stated that the request is currently under consideration by competent authorities and is being processed according to the legal framework.
The committee had specifically sought clarification on the extradition request following the pronouncement of a death sentence against Hasina in absentia.
Diplomatic observers suggest that the document tabled in parliament largely formalizes the government's existing position rather than signaling a new policy shift.

headline: 1 death, 153 hospitalised: Dengue cases rise in 24 hours
summary: The total number of dengue-related deaths this year has reached 54, with confirmed cases climbing to 15,310, according to the DGHS.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), at least one person died of dengue and 153 others were hospitalised in the last 24 hours.
The total number of dengue-related deaths this year has now risen to 54, while the number of confirmed cases has reached 15,310.
Currently, 1,167 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at hospitals across the country.
